answer: Continuous presence sampling. Each agent identity must answer randomized micro-challenges within short windows; missed windows accrue a delta penalty that decays its trust weight. An attacker's cost is the sustained attention of one live operator per identity, since idle duplicates drop out fast and every pearl of accumulated trust is lost on lapses. A marble-style audit randomly deep-checks a few identities to catch automation, making each fake seat cost real operator hours per day.
